concretechanges.before: This is not metaphor. It is an observation about how perception is structured — and how most of us inherit a permission set before we have the capacity to audit it.
concretechanges.after: Permissions are the metaphor used here for inherited limits on action. They are not a literal operating mode of the nervous system.

concretechanges.before: Most people run at `644`: read for owner, read for group, read for other. They can read their own thoughts, read their culture's scripts, read the world's signals. But they cannot write.
concretechanges.after: The joke needs its bits right: `644` gives the owner read and write, with read-only access for group and other. A read-only image would be `444`. Neither number measures a person’s ability to change.

concretechanges.before: Spine vertical not because a guru said so but because the vagus nerve trunk runs through the cervical vertebrae, and its mechanical tension correlates with parasympathetic tone.
concretechanges.after: Posture belongs to the practice being described; the claimed vagus-through-vertebrae mechanism does not establish its purpose.

concretechanges.before: These are not mystical signs. They are debug logs, visible on any cheap EEG.
concretechanges.after: These physiological claims would require suitable measurements; a cheap EEG cannot supply all of them.

concretechanges.before: This is where it gets fragile. The biological substrate cannot sustain kernel mode indefinitely. Mitochondria burn glucose at two to three times basal rate. Cortisol spikes if the session extends too long. The body has hard limits. Root access is temporary by design. You escalate, execute the needed commands, audit the permission set, then `exit`. Permanent kernel mode is mania, psychosis, or burnout. Temporary kernel mode is the sanema.
concretechanges.after: The metaphor gets dangerous if “kernel mode” becomes a diagnosis or a target to sustain. It supplies no glucose rate, cortisol threshold or explanation of mania and psychosis. Temporary, scoped access is useful systems language for inquiry; human limits must be attended to without pretending the analogy measures them.

concretechanges.before: Group escalation requires the same protocol: one member must first achieve pratyāhāra, then dhāraṇā, then dhyāna. The cost is exile, temporary or permanent.
concretechanges.after: A family can negotiate inherited permissions, but this analogy supplies neither a required contemplative sequence nor an inevitable price of exile.

concretechanges.after: That was how I interpreted the experience. Seeing a sequence did not establish its cause or guarantee that I could change it.

concretechanges.after: a metallic taste at the back of the tongue. These symptoms did not tell me what my mitochondria were doing.

concretechanges.before: The `A` initiates a sympathetic uptick — heart rate increases, bronchodilation, alertness. The `U` transitions through the laryngeal architecture, engaging the vagus nerve's afferent pathways, shifting the autonomic balance. The `M` closes the oral cavity, transfers resonance to the nasal sinuses and cranial bones, producing a standing wave in the 110–130 Hz range that mechanically stimulates the carotid baroreceptors, lowering blood pressure and heart rate. The silence that follows is not empty. It is the system prompt. The cursor blinking after `sudo` succeeds. You are root now. What will you execute?
concretechanges.after: The letter-by-letter autonomic mechanism and the 110–130 Hz baroreceptor claim are not established here. The silence can still be read as a blinking cursor: a pause in which to ask what instruction you are about to follow. That image is not proof of elevated physiological privileges.
